{'clinical_notes': "Admission Date: [2845-8-2] Discharge Date: [2845-9-15]
Date of Birth: [2795-5-20] Sex: F
Service: NEUROSURGERY

Chief Complaint: Right-sided hemiparesis, generalized weakness
Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure: Craniotomy for brain tumor resection
History of Present Illness: A 46-year-old female presented with a 2-week history of progressive weakness and right-sided hemiparesis. Patient has a history of hypertension and anxiety. CT scan revealed a large mass in the right frontal lobe. Craniotomy was performed to resect the tumor.
Allergies: NKDA

Past Medical History: Hypertension, Anxiety
Social History: Non-smoker, occasional drinker, homemaker, married with two children

Family History: Father with history of hypertension, mother with history of breast cancer

Physical Exam:
General: Well-developed, well-nourished female in mild distress
Vital signs: BP 120/70 mmHg, HR 82 bpm, RR 16 breaths per minute, Temp 98.6°F, SpO2 98% on room air
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs, rubs, or gallops
Respiratory: Clear to auscultation bilaterally
Abdomen: Soft, non-tender, non-distended
Extremities: Moderate right-sided weakness, intact motor and sensory status
Pertinent Results:

ECG: Normal sinus rhythm
Cardiac enzymes: Elevated troponin levels
CT scan: Mass in right frontal lobe consistent with brain tumor
LP: No effusion noted
Brief Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted for craniotomy to resect a brain tumor due to progressive weakness and right-sided hemiparesis. The procedure was performed successfully, and the patient had an uneventful postoperative course. The patient was started on appropriate medications for blood pressure control and began radiation therapy for brain tumor. The patient's weakness improved significantly, but she still had a mild right-sided hemiparesis on discharge.

Medications on Admission:

Aspirin 81 mg daily
Atorvastatin 40 mg daily
Lisinopril 20 mg daily
Discharge Medications:

Aspirin 81 mg daily
Atorvastatin 40 mg daily
Lisinopril 20 mg daily
Discharge Diagnosis: Brain tumor, Right-sided hemiparesis

Discharge Condition: Stable

Discharge Instructions:

Follow up with neurosurgeon in 2 weeks
Continue medications as prescribed
Monitor blood pressure and report any new symptoms
Follow-up Instructions:
Follow up with neurosurgeon in 2 weeks
